evidence: Varr. LL 10.22: dīrēctōrum genera (Lewis & Short: “in gram., gender”)
Quint. 1.4.23: trādere in nōminibus tria genera
terms.comment: Nouns have three genders, genus masculīnum, fēminīnum, neutrum (Traupman 221). The question goes in the genitive of description: Cujus generis est?, what gender is it?, answered Fēminīnī (Traupman 238). With verbs the same word means voice (see voice).

phrases.latin: nōn erit contentus trādere in nōminibus tria genera et quae sunt duōbus omnibusve commūnia
phrases.english: he will not be content to teach the three genders of nouns and those common to two or to all
How many genders do nouns have?

sources: Lewis & Short: genus
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 221, 238, 246.
